title: Singapore Airlines says 46,000 booking records affected by Amadeus breach
summary: Singapore Airlines joins Cathay Pacific Airways, Japan Airlines, South Korea's Asiana Airlines, and others that have reported customer data ​was compromised in the Amadeus breach

blocks.text: SINGAPORE AIRLINES. A Singapore Airlines Airbus A330-300 plane takes off behind a Boeing 787-10 Dreamliner at Changi Airport in Singapore March 28, 2018.
Singapore Airlines joins Cathay Pacific Airways, Japan Airlines, South Korea's Asiana Airlines, and others that have reported customer data ​was compromised in the Amadeus breach

SINGAPORE – Singapore Airlines said on Tuesday, November 3, that about 46,000 booking records may have been ​affected by a cybersecurity incident involving Amadeus, its reservation technology provider.

The airline joins Cathay Pacific Airways, Japan Airlines, South Korea’s Asiana Airlines, and others that have reported customer data ​was compromised in the Amadeus breach. Malaysia Airlines also said some of its customer information may have been affected
Singapore’s flag carrier said that data exposed by the breach included customers’ names, booking reference numbers, travel itineraries and booking classes
Information including email addresses, phone numbers, travel document details, and KrisFlyer membership numbers may also have been accessed for about 620 booking records, the company said
It added that Amadeus confirmed that bank account or credit card information had not been leaked and bookings were not modified
Singapore Airlines said it was reaching out to affected customers with upcoming travel plans to change their booking reference numbers as a precaution
The airline also confirmed that its IT systems were not breached.
Amadeus ⁠said it had become aware of a vulnerability affecting a travel ​booking display environment but did not ​respond ⁠to a question on how many customers’ data were affected
In recent days, Cathay Pacific and Japan ⁠Airlines ​reported that the breach ​had affected data involving 53,000 bookings and 92,000 customers, respectively – Rappler.com
